headings: S5.3 Outside rearview mirror passenger's side

section.text: S5.3 Outside rearview mirror passenger's side. Each passenger car whose inside rearview mirror does not meet the field of view requirements of S5.1.1 shall have an outside mirror of unit magnification or a convex mirror installed on the passenger's side. The mirror mounting shall provide a stable support and be free of sharp points or edges that could contribute to pedestrian injury. The mirror need not be adjustable from the driver's seat but shall be capable of adjustment by tilting in both horizontal and vertical directions.

fields.description: Demonstrate to a FMVSS compliance inspector that a passenger car with a GVWR of 4,536 kg or less manufactured on or after May 1, 2018, displays a rearview image (a visual image, detected by means of a single source, of the area directly behind the vehicle, provided in a single location to the vehicle operator by means of indirect vision) that meets the requirements of S5.5.1 through S5.5.7. procedure: Confirm the test vehicle is a passenger car with a GVWR of 4,536 kg or less and a manufacture date on or after May 1, 2018, from the vehicle certification label and VIN; record both.
Confirm the rearview image is detected by a single source and displayed in a single location to the operator, per the definition of rearview image.

If the driver has previously modified the field of view (e.g., changed zoom or camera mode), leave that non-default selection in place, then begin a backing event by moving the vehicle direction selector into the reverse position.
Observe that the rearview image meeting S5.5.1 and S5.5.2 appears as the default view at the beginning of the backing event, regardless of the previously selected modification (S5.5.6).

Attach the S14.1 test records demonstrating field of view per S5.5.1 (minimum 150-mm wide portion along the circumference of each test object at positions F and G; full width and height of each test object at positions A through E) and image size per S5.5.2 (average of positions A, B, and C not less than 5 minutes of arc; each individual object not less than 3 minutes of arc).

Video recording of the backing event showing the default rearview image display at event start, its continuous visibility during the backing event, and its disappearance when the backing event ends.
Timed measurement record of response time from start of backing event to compliant image display.
Signed observer record noting the single image source and single display location.

fields.acceptance_criterion: Pass only if the vehicle is a passenger car with a GVWR of 4,536 kg or less manufactured on or after May 1, 2018, and the demonstration and attached records show: (1) the rearview image defaults to the compliant view at the start of each backing event regardless of prior driver modifications (S5.5.6); (2) the compliant image is displayed within 2.0 seconds of the start of a backing event (S5.5.3); (3) the image remains visible during the backing event until the driver modifies the view or the direction selector leaves the reverse position (S5.5.5); (4) the image is not displayed after the backing event has ended (S5.5.4); and (5) attached S14 test records confirm field of view per S5.5.1 (minimum 150-mm wide portion at positions F and G; full width and height at positions A through E), image size per S5.5.2 (average of A, B, C not less than 5 minutes of arc; each not less than 3 minutes of arc), and durability per S5.5.7 after S14.3.1, S14.3.2, and S14.3.3. section.text:
S5.5 Rear visibility.

(a) Phase-in period requirements. For passenger cars with a GVWR of 4,536 kg or less manufactured on or after May 1, 2016, but not later than April 30, 2018, a percentage of each manufacturer's production, as specified in S15, shall display a rearview image meeting the requirements of S5.5.1.

(b) Final requirements. Each passenger car with a GVWR of 4,536 kg or less manufactured on or after May 1, 2018, shall display a rearview image meeting the requirements of S5.5.1 through S5.5.7.

definitions.text: Rearview image means a visual image, detected by means of a single source, of the area directly behind a vehicle that is provided in a single location to the vehicle operator and by means of indirect vision.

references.text:
S5.5.1 Field of view. When tested in accordance with the procedures in S14.1, the rearview image shall include:

(a) A minimum of a 150-mm wide portion along the circumference of each test object located at positions F and G specified in S14.1.4; and

(b) The full width and height of each test object located at positions A through E specified in S14.1.4.

S5.5.2 Size. When the rearview image is measured in accordance with the procedures in S14.1, the calculated visual angle subtended by the horizontal width of

(a) All three test objects located at positions A, B, and C specified in S14.1.4 shall average not less than 5 minutes of arc; and

(b) Each individual test object (A, B, and C) shall not be less than 3 minutes of arc.
S5.5.3 Response time. The rearview image meeting the requirements of S5.5.1 and S5.5.2, when tested in accordance with S14.2, shall be displayed within 2.0 seconds of the start of a backing event.
S5.5.4 Linger time. The rearview image meeting the requirements of S5.5.1 and S5.5.2 shall not be displayed after the backing event has ended.

S5.5.5 Deactivation. The rearview image meeting the requirements of S5.5.1 and S5.5.2 shall remain visible during the backing event until either, the driver modifies the view, or the vehicle direction selector is removed from the reverse position.

S5.5.6 Default view. The rear visibility system must default to the rearview image meeting the requirements of S5.5.1 and S5.5.2 at the beginning of each backing event regardless of any modifications to the field of view the driver has previously selected.
S5.5.7 Durability. The rear visibility system shall meet the field of view and image size requirements of S5.5.1 and S5.5.2 after each durability test specified in S14.3.1, S14.3.2, and S14.3.3.

section.text: S11. Mirror Construction. The average reflectance of any mirror required by this standard shall be determined in accordance with SAE Standard J964 OCT84 (incorporated by reference, see §571.5). All single reflectance mirrors shall have an average reflectance of at least 35 percent. If a mirror is capable of multiple reflectance levels, the minimum reflectance level in the day mode shall be at least 35 percent and the minimum reflectance level in the night mode shall be at least 4 percent. A multiple reflectance mirror shall either be equipped with a means for the driver to adjust the mirror to a reflectance level of at least 35 percent in the event of electrical failure, or achieve such reflectance level automatically in the event of electrical failure.

fields.inspect: Inspect each motorcycle's mirror mounting at the support and attachment points (mirror housing to support, and support to handlebar/body). Because the requirement does not define a measurable limit for "stable," determine with the responsible engineer what measurable criterion applies, e.g. [maximum permitted deflection under a defined hand force in N] or [maximum permitted vibration/drift amplitude]. Note: the source states no numeric limit for stability, so pass/fail against a quantified threshold cannot be determined until the bracketed criterion is defined.

fields.description: Demonstrate to a qualified FMVSS 111 compliance inspector that the rearview image satisfying the S5.5.1 field-of-view and S5.5.2 size requirements is no longer displayed once the backing event has ended. The end of the backing event is at the manufacturer's choosing, per the definition, occurring when vehicle forward motion reaches 10 mph, a distance of 10 meters traveled, or a continuous duration of 10 seconds; the manufacturer's declared end condition must be recorded before the demonstration because it defines when the image is obligated to be off.
procedure: Obtain from the manufacturer the declared backing-event end criterion [manufacturer's declared end condition: 10 mph, 10 meters traveled, or 10 seconds continuous duration] and record it; this choice must be decided and fixed before testing because the source does not state which of the three applies.
Place the vehicle on a flat, unobstructed area and start the vehicle so the rearview image meeting S5.5.1 and S5.5.2 is functional.
Shift the direction selector into reverse and confirm the rearview image is displayed.
Shift the direction selector out of reverse and begin forward motion.

Drive the vehicle until the declared backing-event end condition is reached: (a) forward speed of 10 mph, (b) 10 meters traveled, or (c) a continuous duration of 10 seconds, whichever the manufacturer declared.

From the moment the declared end condition is reached, continuously observe the display location that presented the rearview image and record whether any portion of that rearview image remains visible.
Repeat the sequence a minimum of three times to confirm consistent behavior.
evidence: Continuous video recording of the display during each run, with a synchronized view (or timestamped overlay) showing vehicle speed and distance traveled or elapsed time, covering the moment the declared end condition (10 mph, 10 meters, or 10 seconds) is reached and at least [observation window after end of backing event in seconds] seconds afterward.
Signed observation record stating the manufacturer's declared backing-event end criterion and the result of each of the [minimum number of runs] runs.
fields.acceptance_criterion: In every run, the rearview image meeting the requirements of S5.5.1 and S5.5.2 is displayed while the direction selector is in reverse, and is not displayed at any time after the backing event has ended — i.e., once vehicle forward motion reaches the manufacturer's declared end condition of 10 mph forward speed, 10 meters traveled, or a continuous duration of 10 seconds. Any display of that rearview image after the declared end condition is a fail.

conditions: after each durability test specified in S14.3.1, S14.3.2, and S14.3.3

preconditions: A complete rear visibility system, representative of production, is available and fully functional.

Decide and record whether the three durability tests are applied sequentially to the same sample or to separate samples; the requirement does not state this, so the sample plan must be defined before testing and the same plan used consistently.
A test area per S14.1 (positions A through G and test objects) is arranged and available for field of view and image size measurement.
A salt spray (fog) chamber capable of meeting ASTM B117-03, a humidity/temperature chamber, and a temperature chamber are available and calibrated.
Instruments for measuring rearview image field of view and calculating subtended visual angle per S14.1 are calibrated.
setup: Install the rear visibility system's external components (camera, housing, mount) as installed on the vehicle in normal operating position.
Arrange the S14.1 field of view test setup with test objects at positions A, B, C, D, E, F, and G as specified in S14.1.4.
Position and configure the measurement equipment per the S14.1 procedures to capture and measure the rearview image.

Configure the salt spray chamber to ASTM B117-03 conditions, the humidity chamber to 100° +7°/−0 °F (38° +4°/−0 °C) and 32° +5°/−0 °F (0° +3°/−0 °C), and the temperature chamber to 176° ±5 °F (80° ±3 °C) and 32° +5°/−0 °F (0° +3°/−0 °C).
steps: Establish a baseline: measure the rearview image per S14.1 and record the field of view results and the calculated visual angles subtended by the horizontal widths of test objects at A, B, and C. Record the results.

Apply the S14.3.1 corrosion test: subject the external components to a salt spray (fog) test per ASTM B117-03 for 24 hours. Allow 1 hour to elapse without spray. Repeat for a second 24-hour salt spray cycle.

After the second corrosion cycle, measure the rearview image per S14.1. Record whether the image includes a minimum of a 150-mm wide portion along the circumference of each test object at positions F and G; record whether the image includes the full width and height of each test object at positions A through E; and record the calculated visual angles subtended by the horizontal widths of the test objects at A, B, and C.

Apply the S14.3.2 humidity exposure test: subject the external components to 24 consecutive 3-hour cycles, each consisting of 2 hours at 100° +7°/−0 °F (38° +4°/−0 °C) with relative humidity not less than 90%, followed within not more than 5 minutes by 1 hour at 32° +5°/−0 °F (0° +3°/−0 °C) at humidity not more than 30% ±10%, with no more than 5 minutes between cycles.

After the 24th humidity cycle, measure the rearview image per S14.1. Record the F and G 150-mm visibility results, the A-through-E full width and height visibility results, and the calculated visual angles for test objects A, B, and C.

Apply the S14.3.3 temperature exposure test: subject the external components to 4 consecutive 2-hour cycles, each consisting of 1 hour at 176° ±5 °F (80° ±3 °C), followed within not more than 5 minutes by 1 hour at 32° +5°/−0 °F (0° +3°/−0 °C), with no more than 5 minutes between cycles.

After the 4th temperature cycle, measure the rearview image per S14.1. Record the F and G 150-mm visibility results, the A-through-E full width and height visibility results, and the calculated visual angles for test objects A, B, and C.
Compile the results from all three post-durability measurements and compare each against the S5.5.1 and S5.5.2 criteria.
fields.expected_result: After each of the three durability tests (S14.3.1 corrosion, S14.3.2 humidity, S14.3.3 temperature), the rearview image includes at least a 150-mm wide portion along the circumference of each test object at F and G, includes the full width and height of each test object at A through E, the average of the subtended visual angles of A, B, and C is not less than 5 minutes of arc, and each individual subtended visual angle for A, B, and C is not less than 3 minutes of arc.
fields.pass_criterion: The system passes only if, after each durability test, all of the following are met: (1) field of view includes a minimum of a 150-mm wide portion along the circumference of each test object at positions F and G per S5.5.1(a); (2) field of view includes the full width and height of each test object at positions A through E per S5.5.1(b); (3) the calculated visual angles subtended by the horizontal widths of test objects A, B, and C average not less than 5 minutes of arc per S5.5.2(a); and (4) the calculated visual angle of each individual test object A, B, and C is not less than 3 minutes of arc per S5.5.2(b). The test fails if any of these criteria is not met after any of the three durability tests.

S14.3.1 Corrosion test procedure. The external components are subjected to two 24-hour corrosion test cycles. In each corrosion test cycle, the external components are subjected to a salt spray (fog) test in accordance with ASTM B117-03 (incorporated by reference, see §571.5) for a period of 24 hours. Allow 1 hour to elapse without spray between the two test cycles.

S14.3.2 Humidity exposure test procedure. The external components are subjected to 24 consecutive 3-hour humidity test cycles. In each humidity test cycle, external components are subjected to a temperature of 100° + 7°¥0 °F (38° + 4°¥0 °C) with a relative humidity of not less than 90% for a period of 2 hours. After a period not to exceed 5 minutes, the external components are subjected to a temperature of 32° + 5° ¥0 °F (0° + 3° ¥0 °C) and a humidity of not more than 30% ±10% for 1 hour. Allow no more than 5 minutes to elapse between each test cycle.

S14.3.3 Temperature exposure test procedure. The external components are subjected to 4 consecutive 2-hour temperature test cycles. In each temperature test cycle, the external components are first subjected to a temperature of 176° ±5 °F (80° ±3 °C) for a period of one hour. After a period not to exceed 5 minutes, the external components are subjected to a temperature of 32° + 5° ¥0 °F (0° + 3° ¥0 °C) for 1 hour. Allow no more than 5 minutes to elapse between each test cycle.

setup: Mount the convex mirror rigidly on a stable fixture with the reflective image display facing up or otherwise accessible so the spherometer can be held perpendicular to the convex mirror surface at all required positions.

Identify the image display of the mirror and mark: the center; the left and right ends of a horizontal line that bisects the mirror; and the top and bottom ends of a vertical line that bisects the mirror.

Mark the five locations described in S12.3 on the mirror: at the center of the mirror, at the left and right ends of the horizontal bisecting line, and at the top and bottom ends of the vertical bisecting line.

Verify the 3-point linear spherometer meets S12.2: two outer fixed legs 38 mm apart and one inner movable leg at the midpoint, with a dial indicator scale that can be read accurately to .0025 mm and a zero reading on a flat surface.
Zero the spherometer dial indicator on a flat surface and record that the zero reading is confirmed.
steps: At the center location, orient the spherometer along the horizontal bisecting line, hold it perpendicular to the convex mirror surface, and record the dial indicator reading to the nearest .0025 mm as position 1.

At the center location, rotate the spherometer 90 degrees to the orientation at right angles to position 1, hold it perpendicular to the convex mirror surface, and record the dial indicator reading to the nearest .0025 mm as position 2.

At the left end of the horizontal bisecting line, take a reading with the spherometer in the first orientation, held perpendicular to the mirror surface, and record the dial reading to the nearest .0025 mm as position 3.

At the left end of the horizontal bisecting line, take a reading with the spherometer rotated 90 degrees to the orientation at right angles to position 3, held perpendicular to the mirror surface, and record the dial reading to the nearest .0025 mm as position 4.

At the right end of the horizontal bisecting line, take a reading with the spherometer in the first orientation, held perpendicular to the mirror surface, and record the dial reading to the nearest .0025 mm as position 5.

At the right end of the horizontal bisecting line, take a reading with the spherometer rotated 90 degrees to the orientation at right angles to position 5, held perpendicular to the mirror surface, and record the dial reading to the nearest .0025 mm as position 6.

At the top end of the vertical bisecting line, take a reading with the spherometer in the first orientation, held perpendicular to the mirror surface, and record the dial reading to the nearest .0025 mm as position 7.

At the top end of the vertical bisecting line, take a reading with the spherometer rotated 90 degrees to the orientation at right angles to position 7, held perpendicular to the mirror surface, and record the dial reading to the nearest .0025 mm as position 8.

At the bottom end of the vertical bisecting line, take a reading with the spherometer in the first orientation, held perpendicular to the mirror surface, and record the dial reading to the nearest .0025 mm as position 9.

At the bottom end of the vertical bisecting line, take a reading with the spherometer rotated 90 degrees to the orientation at right angles to position 9, held perpendicular to the mirror surface, and record the dial reading to the nearest .0025 mm as position 10.
Confirm that none of the 10 test positions lies within a 6.4 mm border on the edge of the image display; if any position does, relocate it inward and repeat that reading.

Convert each of the 10 dial readings to a radius of curvature value using Table I of this standard, considering the change as linear for dial readings that fall between two numbers in Table I, in accordance with S12.5, and record each radius of curvature calculation.
Calculate the average radius of curvature by adding all 10 radius of curvature calculations and dividing by ten, in accordance with S12.6, and record the average radius of curvature.
Determine the numerical difference between the average radius of curvature and each of the 10 individual radius of curvature calculations, in accordance with S12.7, and record all 10 differences.

For each of the 10 individual radius of curvature calculations, divide its numerical difference from the average radius of curvature by the average radius of curvature and multiply by 100 to obtain the percentage deviation of each reading from the average.
Record the percentage deviation of each of the 10 readings from the average radius of curvature.
fields.expected_result: Each of the 10 percentage deviations of the individual radii of curvature readings from the average radius of curvature is not more than plus or minus 12.5 percent.
fields.pass_criterion: For each convex mirror tested in accordance with S12, every one of the 10 radii of curvature readings deviates from the average radius of curvature by no more than -12.5 percent and no more than +12.5 percent, i.e., the deviation of each radius of curvature reading from the average radius of curvature is between -12.5 percent and +12.5 percent inclusive. The test fails if any single reading deviates by more than plus or minus 12.5 percent.

section.text: S5.2.2 Mounting. The mirror mounting shall provide a stable support for the mirror, and neither the mirror nor the mounting shall protrude farther than the widest part of the vehicle body except to the extent necessary to produce a field of view meeting or exceeding the requirements of S5.2.1. The mirror shall not be obscured by the unwiped portion of the windshield, and shall be adjustable by tilting in both horizontal and vertical directions from the driver's seated position. The mirror and mounting shall be free of sharp points or edges that could contribute to pedestrian injury.

references.text: S5.2.1 Field of view. Each passenger car shall have an outside mirror of unit magnification. The mirror shall provide the driver a view of a level road surface extending to the horizon from a line, perpendicular to a longitudinal plane tangent to the driver's side of the vehicle at the widest point, extending 2.4 m out from the tangent plane 10.7 m behind the driver's eyes, with the seat in the rearmost position. The line of sight may be partially obscured by rear body or fender contours. The location of the driver's eye reference points shall be those established in Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 104 (§571.104) or a nominal location appropriate for any 95th percentile male driver.

section.text:
S5.5 Rear visibility.

(a) Phase-in period requirements. For passenger cars with a GVWR of 4,536 kg or less manufactured on or after May 1, 2016, but not later than April 30, 2018, a percentage of each manufacturer's production, as specified in S15, shall display a rearview image meeting the requirements of S5.5.1.

(b) Final requirements. Each passenger car with a GVWR of 4,536 kg or less manufactured on or after May 1, 2018, shall display a rearview image meeting the requirements of S5.5.1 through S5.5.7.

definitions.text: Rearview image means a visual image, detected by means of a single source, of the area directly behind a vehicle that is provided in a single location to the vehicle operator and by means of indirect vision.

references.text:
S15 Rear visibility phase-in schedule. For the purposes of the requirements in S15.1 through S15.7, production year means the 12-month period between May 1 of one year and April 30 of the following year, inclusive.

S15.1 Vehicles manufactured on or after May 1, 2016 and before May 1, 2018. At any time during or after the production years ending April 30, 2017 and April 30, 2018, each manufacturer shall, upon request from the Office of Vehicle Safety Compliance, provide information identifying the vehicles (by make, model and vehicle identification number) that have been certified as complying with S5.5.1 or S6.2.1 of this

§571.112

standard. The manufacturer's designation of a vehicle as a certified vehicle is irrevocable.

S15.2 Vehicles manufactured on or after May 1, 2016 and before May 1, 2017. Except as provided in S15.4, for passenger cars, multipurpose passenger vehicles, trucks, buses, and low-speed vehicles with a GVWR of 4,536 kg or less, manufactured by a manufacturer on or after May 1, 2016, and before May 1, 2017, the number of such vehicles complying with S5.5.1 or S6.2.1 shall be not less than 10 percent of the manufacturer's-

(a) Production of such vehicles during that period; or

(b) Average annual production of such vehicles manufactured in the three previous production years.

S15.3 Vehicles manufactured on or after May 1, 2017 and before May 1, 2018. Except as provided in S15.4, for passenger cars, multipurpose passenger vehicles, trucks, buses, and low-speed vehicles with a GVWR of 4,536 kg or less, manufactured by a manufacturer on or after May 1, 2017, and before May 1, 2018, the number of such vehicles complying with S5.5.1 or S6.2.1 shall be not less than 40 percent of the manufacturer's-

(a) Production of such vehicles during that period; or

(b) Average annual production of such vehicles manufactured in the three previous production years.

S15.4 Exclusions from phase-in. The following vehicles shall not be subject to the requirements in S15.1 through S15.3 but shall achieve full compliance with this standard at the end of the phase-in period in accordance with S5.5(b) and S6.2(b):

(a) Vehicles that are manufactured by small manufacturers or by limited line manufacturers.

(b) Vehicles that are altered (within the meaning of 49 CFR 567.7) before May 1, 2017, after having been previously certified in accordance with part 567 of this chapter, and vehicles manufactured in two or more stages before May 1, 2018.

S15.5 Vehicles produced by more than one manufacturer. For the purpose of calculating average annual production of vehicles for each manufacturer and the number of vehicles manufactured by each manufacturer under S15.1 through S15.3, a vehicle produced by more than one manufacturer shall be attributed to a single manufacturer as follows, subject to S15.6-

(a) A vehicle that is imported shall be attributed to the importer.

(b) A vehicle manufactured in the United States by more than one manufacturer, one of which also markets the vehicle, shall be attributed to the manufacturer that markets the vehicle.

S15.6 A vehicle produced by more than one manufacturer shall be attributed to any one of the vehicle's manufacturers specified by an express written contract, reported to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration under 49 CFR part 585, between the manufacturer so specified and the manufacturer to which the vehicle would otherwise be attributed under S15.5.

S15.7 Calculation of complying vehicles. (a) For the purposes of calculating the vehicles complying with S15.2, a manufacturer may count a vehicle if it is manufactured on or after May 1, 2016 but before May 1, 2017.

(b) For purposes of complying with S15.3, a manufacturer may count a vehicle if it is manufactured on or after May 1, 2017 but before May 1, 2018 and,

(c) For the purposes of calculating average annual production of vehicles for each manufacturer and the number of vehicles manufactured by each manufacturer, each vehicle that is excluded from having to meet the applicable requirement is not counted.

preconditions: Vehicle is a passenger car equipped with the rear visibility system (the means of providing the rearview image) installed and operational per production configuration.
Vehicle fuel tank is full (S14.1.2.2).
Any rear hatches or trunk lids are closed and latched in their normal vehicle operating condition (S14.1.2.4).
Vehicle tires are set to the vehicle manufacturer's recommended cold inflation pressure (S14.1.2.1).

Vehicle is loaded to simulate the weight of the driver and four passengers (or designated occupant capacity, if less), with each occupant represented by 45 kg on the seat pan and 23 kg on the vehicle floorboard at the driver's designated seating position and each other available designated seating position (S14.1.2.3).

Driver's seat is adjusted to the midpoint of the longitudinal adjustment range (or the closest position to the rear of midpoint if midpoint is unavailable), to the lowest point of all vertical adjustment ranges, and the seat back angle is set to 25 degrees using the SAE J826 JUL95 manikin, or the closest positional detent toward the manufacturer's nominal design riding position (S14.1.2.5).

setup: Verify test objects F and G are right circular cylinders, 0.8 m high and 0.3 m in external diameter, each marked with a solid vertical stripe of 150 mm width extending from top to bottom, in a color contrasting with both the rest of the cylinder and the test surface (S14.1.3).
Establish a transverse vertical plane tangent to the rearmost surface of the rear bumper (the bumper reference plane).
Place test objects F and G so their centers lie in a transverse vertical plane 0.3 m to the rear of the bumper reference plane (S14.1.4(a)).
Place test object G with its center in a longitudinal vertical plane 1.52 m, measured laterally and horizontally, to the right of the vehicle longitudinal centerline (S14.1.4(e)).
Place test object F with its center in a longitudinal vertical plane 1.52 m, measured laterally and horizontally, to the left of the vehicle longitudinal centerline (S14.1.4(f)).
Orient each test object with its axis vertical.

Establish the test reference point Mr per S14.1.5: locate Mf 635 mm vertically above and 96 mm aft of the H point; locate J 100 mm rearward of Mf and 588 mm above the H point; draw a horizontal line from Mf to J2 (vertically above J); rotate the line about J2 toward the rearview image until the distance from Mf to the center of the display is shortest; this rotated Mf is Mr.

Position a 35 mm or larger format still camera, video camera, or digital equivalent so the center of the camera's image plane is at Mr and the lens is directed at the center of the display's rearview image (S14.1.8(a)); if head restraints obstruct the view, adjust or remove them.
Affix a ruler at the base of the rearview image, oriented perpendicular to a test object cylinder centerline, with a 50 mm delineated section visible in the frame (S14.1.8(b)).
Activate the vehicle's rear visibility system so the live rearview image is displayed.
steps: Measure and record the ambient illumination at the center of the exterior surface of the vehicle's roof and verify it is between 7,000 lux and 10,000 lux.

Verify the lateral and longitudinal placement of test objects F and G relative to the bumper reference plane and the vehicle longitudinal centerline, measuring from the cylindrical center (axis) of each test object as viewed from above, and record the measured positions.
Verify test objects F and G are oriented with their axes vertical and record.
Confirm the driver's seat, vehicle load, tire pressures, fuel level, and closed/latched rear hatches or trunk lids per the preconditions, and record.
Photograph the display with the ruler included in the frame while the rearview image is presented (S14.1.8(c)).

From the photograph, measure the apparent length, along the ruler's edge and near the horizontal center of the rearview image, of the 50 mm delineated section of the ruler (S14.1.8.1(a)) and record it as L_ruler_apparent.
Compute the scaling factor sscale = L_ruler_apparent / 50 mm and record (S14.1.8.2).

From the photograph, measure the apparent horizontal width of the visible portion of the vertical stripe of test object F within the rearview image, at the ruler's edge location, and record it as W_F_apparent.

From the photograph, measure the apparent horizontal width of the visible portion of the vertical stripe of test object G within the rearview image, at the ruler's edge location, and record it as W_G_apparent.
Compute the actual included width for test object F as W_F = W_F_apparent / sscale and record the result in mm.
Compute the actual included width for test object G as W_G = W_G_apparent / sscale and record the result in mm.
Determine the actual distance from Mr to the center of the rearview image (aeye) and record it (S14.1.8.3).

section.text:
S5.5.1 Field of view. When tested in accordance with the procedures in S14.1, the rearview image shall include:

(a) A minimum of a 150-mm wide portion along the circumference of each test object located at positions F and G specified in S14.1.4; and

(b) The full width and height of each test object located at positions A through E specified in S14.1.4.

definitions.text: Rearview image means a visual image, detected by means of a single source, of the area directly behind a vehicle that is provided in a single location to the vehicle operator and by means of indirect vision.

references.text:
S14.1 Field of view and image size test procedure.

S14.1.1 Lighting. The ambient illumination conditions in which testing is conducted consists of light that is evenly distributed from above and is at an intensity of between 7,000 lux and 10,000 lux, as measured at the center of the exterior surface of the vehicle's roof.

S14.1.2 Vehicle conditions.

S14.1.2.1 Tires. The vehicle's tires are set to the vehicle manufacturer's recommended cold inflation pressure.

S14.1.2.2 Fuel tank loading. The fuel tank is full.

S14.1.2.3 Vehicle load. The vehicle is loaded to simulate the weight of the driver and four passengers or the designated occupant capacity, if less. The weight of each occupant is represented by 45 kg resting on the seat pan and 23 kg resting on the vehicle floorboard placed in the driver's designated seating position and any other available designated seating position.

S14.1.2.4 Rear hatch and trunk lids. If the vehicle is equipped with rear hatches or trunk lids, they are closed and latched in their normal vehicle operating condition.

S14.1.2.5 Driver's seat positioning.

S14.1.2.5.1 Adjust the driver's seat to the midpoint of the longitudinal adjustment range. If the seat cannot be adjusted to the midpoint of the longitudinal adjustment range, the closest adjustment position to the rear of the midpoint shall be used.

S14.1.2.5.2 Adjust the driver's seat to the lowest point of all vertical adjustment ranges present.

S14.1.2.5.3 Using the three dimensional SAE Standard J826 JUL95 (incorporated by reference, see §571.5) manikin, adjust the driver's seat back angle at the vertical portion of the Hpoint machine's torso weight hanger to 25 degrees. If this adjustment setting is not available, adjust the seat-back angle to the positional detent setting closest to 25 degrees in the direction of the manufacturer's nominal design riding position.

S14.1.3 Test object. Each test object is a right circular cylinder that is 0.8 m high and 0.3 m in external diameter. There are seven test objects, designated A through G, and they are marked as follows.

(a) Test objects A, B, C, D, and E are marked with a horizontal band encompassing the uppermost 150 mm of the side of the cylinder.

(b) Test objects F and G are marked on the side with a solid vertical stripe of 150 mm width extending from the top to the bottom of each cylinder.

(c) Both the horizontal band and vertical stripe shall be of a color that contrasts with both the rest of the cylinder and the test surface.

S14.1.4 Test object locations and orientation. Place the test objects at locations specified in S14.1.4(a)-(f) and illustrated in Figure 5. Measure the distances shown in Figure 5 from a test object to another test object or other object from the cylindrical center (axis) of the test object as viewed from above. Each test object is oriented so that its axis is vertical.

(a) Place test objects F and G so that their centers are in a transverse vertical plane that is 0.3 m to the rear of a transverse vertical plane tangent to the rearmost surface of the rear bumper.

(b) Place test objects D and E so that their centers are in a transverse vertical plane that is 3.05 m to the rear of a transverse vertical plane tangent to the rearmost surface of the rear bumper.

(c) Place test objects A, B and C so that their centers are in a transverse vertical plane that is 6.1 m to the rear of a transverse vertical plane tangent to the rearmost surface of the rear bumper.

(d) Place test object B so that its center is in a longitudinal vertical plane passing through the vehicle's longitudinal centerline.

(e) Place test objects C, E, and G so that their centers are in a longitudinal vertical plane located 1.52 m, measured laterally and horizontally, to the right of the vehicle longitudinal center line.

(f) Place test objects A, D, and F so that their centers are in a longitudinal vertical plane located 1.52 m, measured laterally and horizontally, to the left of the vehicle longitudinal center line.

S14.1.5 Test reference point. Obtain the test reference point using the following procedure.

(a) Locate the center of the forwardlooking eye midpoint (Mf) illustrated in Figure 6 so that it is 635 mm vertically above the H point (H) and 96 mm aft of the H point.

(b) Locate the head/neck joint center (J) illustrated in Figure 6 so that it is 100 mm rearward of Mf and 588 mm vertically above the H point.

(c) Draw an imaginary horizontal line between Mf and a point vertically above J, defined as J2.

fields.description: Demonstration to an FMVSS 111 compliance observer that the rearview image satisfying the S5.5.1 field-of-view and S5.5.2 size requirements remains visible for the full duration of the backing event, and deactivates only when the driver modifies the view or the vehicle direction selector is removed from the reverse position.
procedure: Confirm before the test that the subject rearview image has been verified (per S5.5.1 and S5.5.2, tested in accordance with S14.1) to include: at least a 150-mm wide portion along the circumference of each test object at positions F and G; the full width and height of each test object at positions A through E; an average visual angle subtended by the horizontal width of test objects A, B, and C of not less than 5 minutes of arc; and a visual angle of not less than 3 minutes of arc for each individual test object A, B, and C. Record the verification report identifiers used as the basis.

Position the vehicle on a flat, open area with sufficient runout for the backing event and place a video camera where it simultaneously captures the rearview image display and the vehicle direction selector (e.g., shifter or selector control).

Verify the ignition is on, the rearview imaging system is in its normal operating state, and the direction selector is in a non-reverse position; confirm the compliant rearview image is not currently displayed.
Move the vehicle direction selector into the reverse position and record the start of the backing event per its definition (backing event begins when the direction selector is placed in reverse).

Observe the display continuously throughout the backing event as the vehicle backs. Note which backing event end condition the manufacturer has selected (vehicle forward motion reaching a speed of 10 mph, a distance of 10 meters traveled, or a continuous duration of 10 seconds) and verify the backing event runs to that endpoint.

While observing, have the driver perform no view modifications and keep the direction selector in reverse; confirm the compliant rearview image remains visible on the display at every observation point from the start of the backing event through its end.

Repeat the backing event. During this repetition, after the image is displayed and the vehicle is backing, have the driver perform one view modification using the manufacturer's view-adjustment control; record the moment the image changes or deactivates.

Repeat the backing event again. During this repetition, with the image displayed and the vehicle backing, have the driver move the direction selector out of the reverse position; record the moment the compliant rearview image is no longer displayed.

Where possible, perform the demonstration such that the observed backing event reaches the manufacturer-selected endpoint while the selector remains in reverse and no view modification is made, demonstrating the image persists until the backing event itself ends rather than deactivating early.
evidence: Continuous time-stamped video of the display and the direction selector for each backing event, showing image visibility from selector placement in reverse through the backing event endpoint and through each deactivation trigger.

Signed observation record noting for each trial: backing event start time, the manufacturer-selected backing event end condition (10 mph speed, 10 meters traveled, or 10 seconds duration) and its observed time, whether the image was visible at every checkpoint, the time of any driver view modification, the time the selector left reverse, and the time the compliant rearview image was no longer visible.
Reference (report ID and date) to the S14.1 field-of-view and size test results (per S5.5.1 and S5.5.2) establishing that the displayed image is the compliant image being demonstrated.
fields.acceptance_criterion: The rearview image verified to meet S5.5.1 and S5.5.2 (150-mm wide portion of each test object at F and G; full width and height of each test object at A through E; average visual angle for A, B, and C of not less than 5 minutes of arc; each of A, B, and C individually not less than 3 minutes of arc) shall remain visible at all times during the backing event whenever the direction selector is in the reverse position and the driver has not modified the view; it may cease to be displayed only after the driver modifies the view or after the vehicle direction selector is removed from the reverse position. The demonstration passes if no disappearance, blanking, or substitution of the image is observed before one of those two events, and the image does deactivate following each of those two events as demonstrated.

section.text: S5.5.5 Deactivation. The rearview image meeting the requirements of S5.5.1 and S5.5.2 shall remain visible during the backing event until either, the driver modifies the view, or the vehicle direction selector is removed from the reverse position.

Backing event means an amount of time which starts when the vehicle's direction selector is placed in reverse, and ends at the manufacturer's choosing, when the vehicle forward motion reaches:

(b) a distance of 10 meters traveled, or

(c) a continuous duration of 10 seconds.

Rearview image means a visual image, detected by means of a single source, of the area directly behind a vehicle that is provided in a single location to the vehicle operator and by means of indirect vision.

S5.5.2 Size. When the rearview image is measured in accordance with the procedures in S14.1, the calculated visual angle subtended by the horizontal width of

(a) All three test objects located at positions A, B, and C specified in S14.1.4 shall average not less than 5 minutes of arc; and

section.text: S5.3 Outside rearview mirror passenger's side. Each passenger car whose inside rearview mirror does not meet the field of view requirements of S5.1.1 shall have an outside mirror of unit magnification or a convex mirror installed on the passenger's side. The mirror mounting shall provide a stable support and be free of sharp points or edges that could contribute to pedestrian injury. The mirror need not be adjustable from the driver's seat but shall be capable of adjustment by tilting in both horizontal and vertical directions.

fields.description: Demonstration to a compliance/verification engineer that, after the driver has changed the selectable field of view, the rear visibility system returns to the default rearview image at the start of every observed backing event and that this default image is the image complying with S5.5.1 and S5.5.2 when evaluated under S14.1.
procedure: Establish reference evidence that the vehicle's default rearview image complies with S5.5.1 and S5.5.2 using S14.1, including the S14.1.4 object positions; record the camera/source, display location, and S14.1 field-of-view and visual-angle results.

For each observed backing event, first end the previous backing event using the manufacturer-declared end condition from the backing-event definition: forward motion reaching 10 mph, 10 meters traveled, or a continuous duration of 10 seconds.

Before the next backing event, use the driver controls to modify the field of view from the default, such as panning, zooming, or selecting a different rear-facing view, and leave that non-default selection active.
Without changing the selection again, place the direction selector in reverse to begin a new backing event.

At the beginning of that backing event, before vehicle motion and before any new driver input, observe the rear visibility display and record whether it presents the default rearview image rather than the previously selected modified field of view.

Compare the displayed default rearview image with the S14.1 reference configuration and results to confirm it is the single-source, single-location rearview image of the area directly behind the vehicle that meets S5.5.1 and S5.5.2.

Repeat the sequence over a representative set of backing events, varying the previously selected field-of-view modifications and including each manufacturer-used backing-event end condition among the observed events.
evidence: Continuous synchronized video showing the direction selector being placed in reverse, the rear visibility display at the start of the backing event, and the prior non-default field-of-view selection still active before reverse is selected.
Still photographs or screen captures of the modified field of view immediately before reverse engagement and the displayed image immediately after reverse engagement.
Vehicle data or synchronized instrumentation showing speed, distance, or continuous duration used to end the prior backing event: 10 mph, 10 meters, or 10 seconds, as applicable.

A signed observation log identifying each backing event, the prior driver-selected field-of-view modification, the manufacturer-declared end condition used, the observer, date/time, and whether the default image appeared at selector placement into reverse.

fields.acceptance_criterion: Pass only if, for every observed backing event and regardless of any field-of-view modification the driver previously selected, the rear visibility system presents the default rearview image at the beginning of the backing event when the direction selector is placed in reverse, before vehicle motion and before any new driver input, after the prior backing event ended at the manufacturer-chosen 10 mph, 10 meters traveled, or 10 seconds condition. section.text: S5.5.6 Default view. The rear visibility system must default to the rearview image meeting the requirements of S5.5.1 and S5.5.2 at the beginning of each backing event regardless of any modifications to the field of view the driver has previously selected.

testability_flags.reason: The horizon is not a fixed, finite point: its distance depends on the driver's eye height and atmospheric visibility, so no finite test can confirm the view actually extends that far and two testers could disagree on whether it does.

preconditions: Vehicle is representative of production, with the inside rearview mirror installed and adjusted to the manufacturer's nominal driving position; the projected eye point is established per §571.104 or at a nominal location appropriate for a 95th percentile male driver as permitted by S5.1.1.
Designated occupant capacity is known; determine the test occupant count as the lesser of five total occupants (driver plus four passengers) or the designated occupant capacity.
A level road surface is available behind the vehicle with surveyed/marked longitudinal distances rearward from the vehicle rear.

The literal horizon check is bounded before verdict: record the program/regulator-decided [specified maximum view distance in m from the rear of the vehicle] to be used in place of an unbounded horizon; if none is decided, the 61 m and 68 kg criteria remain measurable and the horizon-extent portion is recorded as not finite-verifiable.
Ambient visibility and lighting are adequate to distinguish the level road surface and targets through the mirror without adding a numeric visibility limit.
setup: Place the vehicle on the level road surface, rear facing the measured rearward corridor; align the vehicle longitudinal centerline with the surveyed corridor.

Secure occupant-equivalent ballast or anthropomorphic devices at each used seating position so each used position represents an average occupant weight of 68 kg; record the number of used positions and the mass at each position.
Position the driver's eye reference at the §571.104 points or the permitted nominal 95th percentile male driver location; lock the mirror adjustment and mark the eye-point location.

Lay out targets/markers on the level road surface at measured distances rearward from the rear of the vehicle, including the region at and beyond 61 m and out to [specified maximum view distance in m]; record each marker distance.

Install a through-the-mirror camera/eye-point instrument or optical angle-measuring arrangement at the eye point so the reflected field of view can be observed and recorded without moving the eye point during measurement.
Note any partial obscuration by seated occupants or head restraints as permitted by S5.1.1, but do not treat permitted partial obscuration alone as failure.
steps: Verify and record the test occupant count as the lesser of five occupants or the designated occupant capacity, and verify each used position is loaded to represent an average occupant weight of 68 kg.
With the vehicle loaded and the eye point fixed, observe the inside rearview mirror image and identify the nearest point of the level road surface visible in the mirror behind the vehicle.
Measure the longitudinal distance from the rear of the vehicle to that nearest visible level-road point and record it in metres.

Scan the mirror image rearward from that nearest visible point and identify whether the view of the level road surface is continuous out to [specified maximum view distance in m]; record the farthest distance at which the level road surface remains visible and any loss of view.
Measure or compute the vertical angle subtended at the eye point by the visible level-road segment and record it; do not apply a numeric vertical-angle threshold because none is specified in S5.1.1.

Record all locations where seated occupants or head restraints partially obscure the line of sight, and confirm whether the required level-road view is still provided despite those permitted partial obscurations.

Repeat the observation after a normal mirror re-adjustment by the eye-point representative, then restore the original adjustment; record any change in nearest visible distance or farthest visible distance.

fields.pass_criterion: Pass only if the measured nearest visible level-road point is ≤ 61 m to the rear of the vehicle, the occupant loading represents 68 kg average occupant weight for the test occupant count, and the level-road view is continuous from that point through [specified maximum view distance in m]. If [specified maximum view distance in m] has not been decided, the 61 m and 68 kg criteria may be judged, but the horizon-extent portion cannot be given a finite pass verdict.

fields.description: Demonstration that the driver's-side outside rearview mirror is adjustable by tilting in both the horizontal and vertical directions from the driver's seated position. An engineer or inspector sits in the driver's seat and personally operates the mirror adjustment through its full range while a second observer confirms the motion.
procedure: Position the driver's seat at the design driving position for a 50th-percentile adult driver; if the seat is adjustable, set it to a mid-track position and record the settings.
Verify the outside rearview mirror assembly is installed and fully functional on the driver's side of the vehicle, in accordance with S5.2.2 Mounting.

Have the inspector sit in the driver's seat and, without leaving the seated position or using any tool or access outside normal reach, grasp or operate the mirror-adjustment control or the mirror housing directly as intended by design.
While remaining seated, tilt the mirror through its full range in the horizontal direction (left to right) and confirm the reflected field of view visibly changes in azimuth.
While remaining seated, tilt the mirror through its full range in the vertical direction (up to down) and confirm the reflected field of view visibly changes in elevation.
Repeat each tilt direction at least once and return the mirror to a usable driving position.
Record the observations on the demonstration record, signed by the seated inspector and the observer.
evidence: Video showing the inspector seated in the driver's seat tilting the mirror through its full horizontal range, with the reflected image visibly changing left to right.
Video or time-lapse photographs showing the inspector seated in the driver's seat tilting the mirror through its full vertical range, with the reflected image visibly changing up to down.

Signed observation record naming the vehicle, mirror tested, seat position settings, date, and the inspector's and observer's confirmations that both tilt directions were achieved without the inspector leaving the seated position.
fields.acceptance_criterion: Pass if, while the inspector remains in the driver's seated position with no tools and no access beyond normal reach, the mirror visibly tilts through its full range in both the horizontal direction (left to right) and the vertical direction (up and down), changing the reflected field of view in each direction. Fail if the mirror cannot be tilted in either direction, the range of motion in either direction is visibly absent, or the inspector must leave the seated position to make the adjustment. The requirement states no numeric angular range, so no degree limit is applied.

section.text: S5.2.2 Mounting. The mirror mounting shall provide a stable support for the mirror, and neither the mirror nor the mounting shall protrude farther than the widest part of the vehicle body except to the extent necessary to produce a field of view meeting or exceeding the requirements of S5.2.1. The mirror shall not be obscured by the unwiped portion of the windshield, and shall be adjustable by tilting in both horizontal and vertical directions from the driver's seated position. The mirror and mounting shall be free of sharp points or edges that could contribute to pedestrian injury.

preconditions: Vehicle is a passenger car equipped with the rear visibility system that produces the rearview image (a visual image of the area directly behind the vehicle, provided in a single location to the vehicle operator by means of indirect vision).
Vehicle's tires are set to the vehicle manufacturer's recommended cold inflation pressure (S14.1.2.1).
Vehicle's fuel tank is full (S14.1.2.2).

Vehicle is loaded to simulate the driver and four passengers (or the designated occupant capacity, if less), with each occupant represented by 45 kg on the seat pan and 23 kg on the vehicle floorboard, placed in the driver's designated seating position and any other available designated seating position (S14.1.2.3).
If the vehicle is equipped with rear hatches or trunk lids, they are closed and latched in their normal vehicle operating condition (S14.1.2.4).

Driver's seat is adjusted to the midpoint of the longitudinal adjustment range, or if unavailable, to the closest adjustment position to the rear of the midpoint (S14.1.2.5.1); to the lowest point of all vertical adjustment ranges (S14.1.2.5.2); and the seat-back angle is set to 25 degrees using the SAE J826 JUL95 H-point manikin, or to the positional detent closest to 25 degrees in the direction of the manufacturer's nominal design riding position (S14.1.2.5.3).

The steering wheel is adjusted so the longitudinal centerline of all vehicle tires is parallel to the vehicle longitudinal centerline, or if no such position exists, to the position where the tire centerlines are closest to parallel (S14.1.7).
Rearview image system is operating normally and displaying the rearview image.
setup: Conduct the test at an ambient illumination between 7,000 lux and 10,000 lux, evenly distributed from above, measured at the center of the exterior surface of the vehicle's roof (S14.1.1). Record the measured illumination.

Place seven right circular cylinder test objects, each 0.8 m high and 0.3 m in external diameter (S14.1.3). Mark test objects A, B, C, D, and E with a horizontal band encompassing the uppermost 150 mm of the side of the cylinder, and test objects F and G with a solid vertical stripe of 150 mm width extending from top to bottom; all marks in a color contrasting with both the rest of the cylinder and the test surface (S14.1.3(a)-(c)).

Establish a transverse vertical plane tangent to the rearmost surface of the rear bumper. Measure all placement distances from the cylindrical center (axis) of each test object as viewed from above, and orient each test object with its axis vertical (S14.1.4).
Place test objects D and E with their centers in a transverse vertical plane 3.05 m to the rear of the plane tangent to the rear bumper (S14.1.4(b)).
Place test objects A, B, and C with their centers in a transverse vertical plane 6.1 m to the rear of the plane tangent to the rear bumper (S14.1.4(c)).
Place test object B with its center in a longitudinal vertical plane passing through the vehicle's longitudinal centerline (S14.1.4(d)).
Place test objects C and E with their centers in a longitudinal vertical plane located 1.52 m, measured laterally and horizontally, to the right of the vehicle longitudinal centerline (S14.1.4(e)).

Place test object A (and, for completeness of the layout, D) with its center in a longitudinal vertical plane located 1.52 m, measured laterally and horizontally, to the left of the vehicle longitudinal centerline (S14.1.4(f)). Positions F and G are laid out per S14.1.4(a) but are not evaluated under this requirement.

Locate the center of the forward-looking eye midpoint (Mf) 635 mm vertically above the H point and 96 mm aft of the H point; locate the head/neck joint center (J) 100 mm rearward of Mf and 588 mm vertically above the H point; draw an imaginary horizontal line from Mf to J2 (a point vertically above J); rotate this line about J2 toward the rearview image until the straight-line distance from Mf to the center of the display reaches its shortest possible value, and define this rotated location as Mr (S14.1.5).
If the display has a rotational adjustment mechanism, adjust the display surface to be normal to the imaginary line through Mr and J2, or as near to normal as the adjustment allows (S14.1.6).

Position a 35 mm or larger format still camera, video camera, or digital equivalent so that the center of the camera's image plane is at Mr and the lens is directed at the center of the display's rearview image (S14.1.8(a)).

Affix a ruler with a delineated 50 mm section at the base of the rearview image, oriented perpendicular to a test object cylinder centerline; if head restraints obstruct the view of the display, adjust or remove them (S14.1.8(b)).
steps: Display the rearview image and photograph the visual display with the ruler included in the frame (S14.1.8(c)). Record the photograph.

From the photograph, measure the apparent length of the 50 mm delineated section of the ruler along the ruler's edge, closest to the rearview image and near the horizontal center of the rearview image (S14.1.8.1(a)). Record this apparent length.
Compute the scaling factor sscale by dividing the apparent length of the 50 mm ruler section by 50 mm (S14.1.8.2). Record sscale.
Determine the actual distance from Mr to the center of the rearview image (aeye) and record it (S14.1.8.3).

Using the photograph and the scaling factor sscale, measure for each of test objects A, B, C, D, and E: (a) the apparent horizontal width of the visible cylinder image at its widest point, and (b) the apparent vertical height of the visible cylinder image from its lowest visible point to its highest visible point. Convert each apparent measurement to object-equivalent dimensions by dividing by sscale. Record width and height for each of the five test objects.

For each of test objects A, B, C, D, and E, examine the photograph to confirm whether the full left and right edges (sides) and the full top and bottom of the cylinder image are visible within the boundaries of the rearview image, or whether any part of the cylinder image is cut off or cropped by an edge of the rearview image. Record 'full outline visible' or 'cropped' for each object.
fields.expected_result: The rearview image shows the complete outline of each of the five test objects A through E: the entire width (the full 0.3 m external diameter) and the entire height (the full 0.8 m) of each cylinder is visible within the rearview image, with no part of any cylinder image cropped by the image boundary.
fields.pass_criterion: For each of the five test objects A through E: (1) the measured visible width, converted to object-equivalent units using sscale, is equal to 0.3 m (recorded measured value ≥ 0.3 m, allowing for only measurement/readability uncertainty of the photograph, since any cropping would reduce the measured width below 0.3 m); (2) the measured visible height, converted to object-equivalent units using sscale, is equal to 0.8 m (recorded measured value ≥ 0.8 m, allowing for only measurement/readability uncertainty of the photograph, since any cropping would reduce the measured height below 0.8 m); and (3) the full left edge, right edge, top, and bottom of each cylinder image lie within the rearview image boundaries (no cropping recorded for any of objects A through E). The test fails if any of these criteria is not met for any one of test objects A, B, C, D, or E.

section.text:
S5.5.1 Field of view. When tested in accordance with the procedures in S14.1, the rearview image shall include:

(a) A minimum of a 150-mm wide portion along the circumference of each test object located at positions F and G specified in S14.1.4; and

(b) The full width and height of each test object located at positions A through E specified in S14.1.4.

definitions.text: Rearview image means a visual image, detected by means of a single source, of the area directly behind a vehicle that is provided in a single location to the vehicle operator and by means of indirect vision.

references.text:
S14.1 Field of view and image size test procedure.

S14.1.1 Lighting. The ambient illumination conditions in which testing is conducted consists of light that is evenly distributed from above and is at an intensity of between 7,000 lux and 10,000 lux, as measured at the center of the exterior surface of the vehicle's roof.

S14.1.2 Vehicle conditions.

S14.1.2.1 Tires. The vehicle's tires are set to the vehicle manufacturer's recommended cold inflation pressure.

S14.1.2.2 Fuel tank loading. The fuel tank is full.

S14.1.2.3 Vehicle load. The vehicle is loaded to simulate the weight of the driver and four passengers or the designated occupant capacity, if less. The weight of each occupant is represented by 45 kg resting on the seat pan and 23 kg resting on the vehicle floorboard placed in the driver's designated seating position and any other available designated seating position.

S14.1.2.4 Rear hatch and trunk lids. If the vehicle is equipped with rear hatches or trunk lids, they are closed and latched in their normal vehicle operating condition.

S14.1.2.5 Driver's seat positioning.

S14.1.2.5.1 Adjust the driver's seat to the midpoint of the longitudinal adjustment range. If the seat cannot be adjusted to the midpoint of the longitudinal adjustment range, the closest adjustment position to the rear of the midpoint shall be used.

S14.1.2.5.2 Adjust the driver's seat to the lowest point of all vertical adjustment ranges present.

S14.1.2.5.3 Using the three dimensional SAE Standard J826 JUL95 (incorporated by reference, see §571.5) manikin, adjust the driver's seat back angle at the vertical portion of the Hpoint machine's torso weight hanger to 25 degrees. If this adjustment setting is not available, adjust the seat-back angle to the positional detent setting closest to 25 degrees in the direction of the manufacturer's nominal design riding position.

S14.1.3 Test object. Each test object is a right circular cylinder that is 0.8 m high and 0.3 m in external diameter. There are seven test objects, designated A through G, and they are marked as follows.

(a) Test objects A, B, C, D, and E are marked with a horizontal band encompassing the uppermost 150 mm of the side of the cylinder.

(b) Test objects F and G are marked on the side with a solid vertical stripe of 150 mm width extending from the top to the bottom of each cylinder.

(c) Both the horizontal band and vertical stripe shall be of a color that contrasts with both the rest of the cylinder and the test surface.

S14.1.4 Test object locations and orientation. Place the test objects at locations specified in S14.1.4(a)-(f) and illustrated in Figure 5. Measure the distances shown in Figure 5 from a test object to another test object or other object from the cylindrical center (axis) of the test object as viewed from above. Each test object is oriented so that its axis is vertical.

(a) Place test objects F and G so that their centers are in a transverse vertical plane that is 0.3 m to the rear of a transverse vertical plane tangent to the rearmost surface of the rear bumper.

(b) Place test objects D and E so that their centers are in a transverse vertical plane that is 3.05 m to the rear of a transverse vertical plane tangent to the rearmost surface of the rear bumper.

(c) Place test objects A, B and C so that their centers are in a transverse vertical plane that is 6.1 m to the rear of a transverse vertical plane tangent to the rearmost surface of the rear bumper.

(d) Place test object B so that its center is in a longitudinal vertical plane passing through the vehicle's longitudinal centerline.

(e) Place test objects C, E, and G so that their centers are in a longitudinal vertical plane located 1.52 m, measured laterally and horizontally, to the right of the vehicle longitudinal center line.

(f) Place test objects A, D, and F so that their centers are in a longitudinal vertical plane located 1.52 m, measured laterally and horizontally, to the left of the vehicle longitudinal center line.

S14.1.5 Test reference point. Obtain the test reference point using the following procedure.

(a) Locate the center of the forwardlooking eye midpoint (Mf) illustrated in Figure 6 so that it is 635 mm vertically above the H point (H) and 96 mm aft of the H point.

(b) Locate the head/neck joint center (J) illustrated in Figure 6 so that it is 100 mm rearward of Mf and 588 mm vertically above the H point.

procedure: Confirm the mirror and mounting are production-representative and are installed on the vehicle or fixture configuration applicable to S5.1.2; record the configuration.

section.text: S5.1.2 Mounting. The mirror mounting shall provide a stable support for the mirror, and shall provide for mirror adjustment by tilting in both the horizontal and vertical directions. If the mirror is in the head impact area, the mounting shall deflect, collapse or break away without leaving sharp edges when the reflective surface of the mirror is subjected to a force of 400 N in any forward direction that is not more than 45° from the forward longitudinal direction.

steps: Classify the mirror type: a mirror of unit magnification (flat) or a convex mirror (curved reflective surface with the shape of the exterior surface of a section of a sphere, per the definition). Record the classification.

For a convex mirror, determine the reflective surface area in mm 2 using the same method. Record the area.

For a convex mirror, measure the average radius of curvature in mm by taking radius-of-curvature readings at multiple locations across the reflective surface and averaging them (e.g., with a spherometer or equivalent instrument). Record each reading and the average.

section.text: S11. Mirror Construction. The average reflectance of any mirror required by this standard shall be determined in accordance with SAE Standard J964 OCT84 (incorporated by reference, see §571.5). All single reflectance mirrors shall have an average reflectance of at least 35 percent. If a mirror is capable of multiple reflectance levels, the minimum reflectance level in the day mode shall be at least 35 percent and the minimum reflectance level in the night mode shall be at least 4 percent. A multiple reflectance mirror shall either be equipped with a means for the driver to adjust the mirror to a reflectance level of at least 35 percent in the event of electrical failure, or achieve such reflectance level automatically in the event of electrical failure.
